title: Release Doorway: Gatekeeper Checks for LTS & Incremental Upgrade Paths
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Implement a "gatekeeper" release doorway that automatically runs a compact, high-signal validation suite for every candidate runtime and service release, with special handling for LTS channel promotions and incremental upgrade paths. The doorway is intended to be the single automated decision point before allowing a release to proceed to canary, dedicated-channel, or LTS promotion. It must cover fast smoke checks, lightweight performance regression gates, structured evals for user-visible regressions, and upgrade compatibility checks for Private/VPC/on-prem environments.

Goals:
- Prevent obvious regressions from progressing into canary or LTS channels.
- Ensure upgrade compatibility across minor version bumps and produce clear rollback criteria.
- Keep the doorway run time under a practical SLA so it can be part of CI (target: <= 45 minutes for fast path, longer offline checks allowed for full LTS promotion).
- Integrate with existing rollout tooling: canary percent policy, automatic fallback, and rollout dashboards.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full long-duration soak tests or exhaustive evals for all downstream customer workloads; those live in the nightly LTS certification pipeline.

Key constraints and considerations:
- LTS promotions must include an extra offline "certify" step that runs extended perf sweeps and security scans; the doorway only gates the fast-path promotion to canary and dedicated channels.
- Private deployments require a dry-run mode that can validate KMS/HSM interactions, network policies, and upgrade playbooks without applying changes.
- Metric baselines come from the last GA runtime in the same minor channel; if baseline is missing, the doorway will use the most recent stable candidate and mark the run as "baseline-missing" requiring manual review.

Primary deliverables:
- A CLI/CI job "release-doorway-runner" that executes the validations and emits a JSON verdict with metrics and signal buckets (smoke, perf, eval, compatibility).
- A set of standardized thresholds and a JSON schema for the verdict to be consumed by the rollout-orchestrator.
- Dashboard tiles and alerts for doorway failures with links to run artifacts and diffs.
- Documentation: runbook for on-call and an LTS promotion checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Automated doorway job exists and can be invoked from CI (git tag or PR) and returns pass/fail JSON
Failure conditions are enforced by the release pipeline so failing doorway blocks canary promotion
Smoke tests cover core API flows (generation, streaming, embeddings, kv-cache warm path) and must be green
Perf regression gate: p95 latency regression <= 7% and throughput drop <= 8% against baseline; failures must produce a diff report
Memory and GPU utilization increases limited to < 10% for the same workload; larger increases mark candidate as high-risk
Eval suite runs a set of curated prompts (sanity, hallucination, formatting) and flags content-regressions with examples
Doorway runtime for the fast path completes in <= 45 minutes in CI (when cached artifacts available)
Dry-run compatibility check for Private installs validates KMS handshake, config migration, and package install simulation
Verdict JSON adheres to the defined schema and is consumable by release-orchestrator for automated gating
Documentation and runbook published with a clear rollback procedure and post-failure checklist
test_matrix: Smoke: quick end-to-end generation and streaming (3 scenarios) on a representative instance (cpu/gpu)
Perf: microbench P95 latency and throughput on 3 model sizes (small/medium/large) using BenchDB harness
Evals: 50 curated prompts for output regressions, structural validation, and tool-calling correctness
Upgrade path: dry-run of in-place minor upgrade, config migration checks, and KV cache warm-start test
LTS promotion: extended perf sweep (1h), security scan, and backward-compatibility assertions
Canary gating: progressive rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic stop on signal violation
automation_tasks: Add release-doorway-runner job to CI config and make it a required status check
Publish verdict JSON schema to schemas/release/verdict-v1.json in the repo
Wire verdict outputs to rollout-orchestrator to enable automatic canary blocking
Create dashboard panel that maps failing doorway runs by release, commit, and owner
Implement private/dry-run adapter that performs compatibility checks without applying state changes
Add a small synthetic workload generator for perf runs to reduce noise and keep run times low
